never-told.subject: a diary with a padlock bigger than it needs
never-told.why: the thing you write in and lock; at 25×30 the padlock is what you read, the book is behind it
never-told.xs: the padlock alone (body, shackle, keyhole): the key shape
never-told.from: b-riso, redrawn (a padlock bigger than the diary it locks is the key shape)

off-chest.subject: a kettle at the boil, lid lifted off by the steam
off-chest.why: letting it out (Dampf ablassen, 吐き出す): the pressure has to go somewhere; the lid floats, the steam puff is the second ink
off-chest.xs: the kettle body with spout and lid

guilty.subject: a cookie with a bite out of it, two crumbs
guilty.why: caught: the evidence is in your hand; the bite is the confession

hot-take.subject: one chili pepper, curved, with its cap and stem
hot-take.why: spicy / scharf / 辛口 / pedas: 'hot opinion' is the same idiom in all nine languages
hot-take.xs: the fat pod with its cap

cringe.subject: someone gone headfirst into the ground, one leg still kicking
cringe.why: the idiom all nine markets share: earth, swallow me / 穴があったら入りたい / 쥐구멍 / tierra trágame / im Erdboden versinken; funny, no face
cringe.xs: the ground and the two legs with their shoes
cringe.from: b-riso, redrawn (one leg kicking at the knee, shoes sole-up, so the legs read as legs and not sprouts)

pretending.subject: a smiling mask held up on a stick (the set's one face, and it is a mask)
pretending.why: the fine face you hold up in front of the real one; the stick says held, not worn
pretending.xs: the mask with two eye holes and the stick
pretending.from: b-riso, redrawn (a held mask, not an emoji: cheekbones, almond eyes, a stick)

almost-texted.subject: a typing bubble with three dots, over the top edge of a phone
almost-texted.why: the draft that never gets sent: the dots are punched out, the phone only shows its top
almost-texted.xs: bubble with dots + the phone edge

situationship.subject: two socks, toes toward each other, one striped and one plain: not a pair
situationship.why: 'almost a pair' is the whole situation; the mismatch does the talking without a heart

not-over-it.subject: their hoodie, still on the hanger in your wardrobe
not-over-it.why: the thing you kept (まだ引きずってる): a garment and a hook, no heart with a crack
not-over-it.xs: hood, body and sleeves as one shape

unsent.subject: an envelope standing in an open drawer
unsent.why: the letter that stayed in the drawer (出さなかった手紙, nie abgeschickt): not thrown away, not sent
unsent.xs: envelope on the drawer, flap as a notch
unsent.from: b-riso, tuned (bigger envelope, deeper in the drawer)

crush.subject: a folded note slipped under a door
crush.why: the lead's own example: specific, shy, no heart
crush.xs: door and note as one piece

what-if.subject: a die balanced on one corner, not landed yet
what-if.why: the version where it fell the other way: the roll is still undecided; a die is chance in every market, the tilt makes it this moment
what-if.xs: the tilted die with three pips
what-if.from: graft: the die (a-keepsakes, c-scenes), redrawn as a cut-paper die balanced on one corner

overthinking.subject: a ball of yarn with the end trailing off
overthinking.why: the tangle you keep winding (dándole vueltas, 頭がこんがらがる); the loose end is the thought you can't put down

cant-sleep.subject: one sheep, standing, wide awake
cant-sleep.why: the sheep that did not work; counting sheep is known in all nine markets, and a sheep on a navy stamp is nobody's icon font
cant-sleep.xs: the fluffy body with the head and two legs
cant-sleep.from: b-riso, tuned (an open eye: wide awake)

intrusive.subject: a toaster that has just popped, the slice flying out
intrusive.why: it comes up by itself, loudly, when nothing asked it to (불쑥, hereingeplatzt, 勝手に浮かぶ)
intrusive.xs: the toaster and the slice above it
intrusive.from: graft: the toaster (a-keepsakes), redrawn as a cut-paper toaster and a slice in mid-air

whats-the-point.subject: an empty ice-cream cone, the scoop fallen on the floor beside it
whats-the-point.why: the small tragedy that makes you ask 'what for'; readable in every market, sad-funny rather than bleak

spiral.subject: a washing machine on spin, the drum's swirl in the porthole
spiral.why: the loop that will not stop until the cycle ends (ぐるぐる, Kopfkarussell, on spin cycle); a thing you hear at 3am, not a hypnosis spiral
spiral.xs: the machine with its porthole and the drum's centre
spiral.from: new (director): none of the three spirals survived next to the yarn ball or the cone

too-honest.subject: a bare bulb on its cord, no shade
too-honest.why: nothing between you and the light: the unfiltered hour (3am), said without a lampshade on it
too-honest.xs: cord, cap and bulb as one mark
too-honest.from: graft: the bare bulb (a-keepsakes), redrawn as a cut-paper bulb with its filament

made-my-day.subject: a ladybug that landed on you
made-my-day.why: the smallest good thing, and luck in de/fr/it/ja/ko; dome, spots and the wing cut read at 25
made-my-day.xs: the dome split by the wing gap, two spots

ordinary.subject: a mug with the teabag string and tag hanging over the rim
ordinary.why: an ordinary day is a cup of tea; the tag makes it this cup, not the mug icon

a-song.subject: a record pulled half out of its sleeve, its label printed in the second ink
a-song.why: the one you keep putting back on; vinyl is Gen-Z's own revival, and a record half out of its sleeve is a thing, not the music-note icon
a-song.xs: the record alone, with its label hole
a-song.from: graft: the record (c-scenes' turntable, the owner's own reference), redrawn as a record sliding out of its sleeve, the label in the second ink

outside.subject: a snail after rain, horns up
outside.why: something you actually see outside and stop for; the shell's spiral is a cut, not a stroke
outside.xs: shell on its foot with the horns

comfort.subject: a bowl of soup with the spoon in it, one curl of steam
comfort.why: comfort food is comfort in every market; the steam curl is the second ink
comfort.xs: bowl, foot and a fat spoon

tiny-win.subject: a made bed
tiny-win.why: a win nobody else would notice; universal, dry, Gen-Z (ja/de read it the same)

growing.subject: a plant that has cracked its small pot
growing.why: still figuring it out: the pot stayed the size it was, the plant did not
growing.from: b-riso, tuned (the pot is cracked: it really has been outgrown)

changed.subject: open scissors and the lock of hair they just cut
changed.why: new hair, new me: the 2am haircut is the quickest way anyone announces they are different now
changed.from: graft: scissors and the lock they just cut (a-keepsakes, c-scenes), redrawn as cut paper

lost.subject: a signpost with two blank boards pointing opposite ways, the top one hanging askew
lost.why: the not-knowing: arrows that point and say nothing; the drooping board is the joke
lost.from: graft: the signpost with blank boards (a-keepsakes, c-scenes), redrawn as cut paper, top board askew

big-feeling.subject: one wave rearing up and curling over, two drops of spray
big-feeling.why: a wave of feeling is the same idiom in all nine languages (ola, Welle, vague, onda, gelombang, 波, 파도); too big to name, drawn at the size it feels
big-feeling.from: graft: the breaking wave (c-scenes), redrawn as one cut-paper curl

letting-go.subject: a birdcage with its door swung open and nobody inside, one feather drifting up
letting-go.why: the act of letting go in the app's own language: the bird is already out, carrying something
letting-go.xs: the cage, its base and the open door
letting-go.from: graft: the open birdcage (c-scenes), redrawn with a cut-paper base and door; the feather is the second ink

who-am-i.subject: the tall arched mirror standing in every bedroom, nothing in it but the glare
who-am-i.why: trying to figure yourself out happens in front of this mirror; empty glass, two glare lines, no face
who-am-i.xs: the arched frame on its floor line
who-am-i.from: b-riso's mirror idea, redrawn as the arched floor mirror (so it is not the search glyph)

miss-someone.subject: an empty chair
miss-someone.why: the second face of the old set goes; the place where someone sat says it in every language

homesick.subject: a little house inside a snow globe
homesick.why: home kept under glass, far and small; the house is a cut, the globe is the shape
homesick.xs: globe and base with the house cut

grief.subject: a tulip bowed right over, one petal already on the ground
grief.why: loss without a candle or a dove: a flower that has let its head drop; the fallen petal is the second ink

then-now.subject: a cassette tape
then-now.why: the way things used to be, in the object that held them; two reel holes and the label read at any size
then-now.xs: the shell with two reel holes
then-now.from: graft: the cassette (a-keepsakes, c-scenes; 📼 is this stamp's own emoji), in b-riso's cut

old-friend.subject: a paper-cup telephone, the string gone slack between the two cups
old-friend.why: someone I drifted from: the line is still there, it just sags
old-friend.xs: the two cups and the sagging string
old-friend.from: graft: the paper-cup telephone (a-keepsakes), redrawn as two cut-paper cups and a slack string

seasons.subject: a tree, leafy on one side and bare on the other
seasons.why: the year turning in one silhouette; works where there is no autumn too; the falling leaf is the second ink
seasons.xs: trunk, the leafy half and the main branch
